column1: # html-dialog-v1-gold labels of html-dialog-v1 (Issue #113), read only by the scorer. Same label columns and syntax as html-decision-v1 gold.tsv.

# goldRef names the html-decision-v1 case whose adjudicated label (html-decision-v1-gold-v2) the turn reuses; its resolved constraints and candidates must equal that case's, and its label columns are '-'.
# change (first|revise|qualify|keep|any) and withoutContext (same|abstain) are checked against the labels at load. Inline labels are drafted by the rule author and not independently adjudicated.

column11: The first turn asks how to run JavaScript but states no constraint that separates inline code, an external file, defer or a module; the answer is to ask, for example whether the code is a module.

The policy allows the site's own script files but blocks inline code, so a same-origin external classic script is required; reuse across pages favours the external file too. defer stays acceptable because immediate execution is not required, inline code is now blocked, and the code is not a module.
Every stated constraint allows several loading modes; whether the script must wait for the parsed document decides between a plain external file and external+defer, so the answer is to ask that.

Turn 2 stated that the order of the features means nothing; turn 3 states that it matters without marking a change. The requirements contradict each other, and order is exactly what separates ol from ul, so the answer is to ask which holds.

Whether an untrusted third party is safe to embed is outside the html-decision-v1 rubric: no constraint and no host rule covers sandboxing or origin trust, so no candidate can be recommended as secure from the rubric. The supported answer is to say so instead of repeating the earlier iframe advice.
The first and only turn is an ellipsis without an antecedent: nothing says what 'it' is or which choice is meant, so the answer is to ask.

The turn refers back to the articles of turn 1, but the host supplied only turn 2, which states no family or document requirement; without the earlier turn the question is under-specified and the answer is to ask.
The carried context exceeds the dialog-context byte budget. A bounded host must say that it cannot use the whole context rather than silently drop part of it, so no recommendation is made.
